key_insight: Biomedical claim-verification agents need relevant evidence, not merely valid citations: retrieval was the main bottleneck in this study.
clinical_relevance: Scientific assistants used in medicine should check whether cited papers support a claim, because a real PubMed ID does not establish relevance.
method: Evaluated SciFact claim verification with two language-model backbones and live PubMed search as the only tool.
Compared closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval, agent-written queries, and an oracle supplied with gold abstracts.
Audited citation existence and relevance using a cross-family LLM judge.
evidence_signal: Agent-written queries achieved 62% accuracy versus 49–59% for other realistic harnesses, without statistically significant differences; gold abstracts yielded 79–86%, while only 3 of 327 existing closed-book citations were judged relevant.
watch_item: The benchmark sample limited statistical power, and citation relevance was assessed by an LLM judge rather than established through clinical validation.
paper_title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
